title: Integration description
description: What <program> describe prints on its standard output, once, as one JSON document, and exits 0: the integration's name, the settings it takes and the roles it plays. It takes no settings and reaches no network. A program that fails prints nothing on standard output, one line on standard error naming what failed, and exits non-zero. A reader expands a declared integration into its definitions from this document, so the reader holds no table of integrations.

name.description: The integration's name: the key a machine's configuration declares it under, unless the machine chooses another, and so the name of what it defines there. The key names the runner's credential and the program qory-<key> of this repository's, so the name is the credential's grammar without the dot.

title.description: A human name, for a form or a listing.

description.description: A sentence or two on what the integration does, for a form or a listing.

program_version.description: The program's own version, as it was built.

settings.description: A JSON Schema, draft 2020-12, of the settings document: an object. A property marked writeOnly is a secret: a form shows it as one, nothing logs it, and no command line carries it. A secret is a property of the settings object itself, never a nested one, and a secret <name> has a setting <name>_file, a file that holds it, which a command line carries in its place.

roles.description: The roles the program plays, by name. A reader ignores a role it does not know. The tool, work_source and output roles come with contracts of their own and are not defined yet.

credential.description: The runner's credential adapter. The program is started as <program> credential --settings <json> -- <argument> and prints the runner's credential document.

argument.description: A regular expression, RE2, the policy's argument must match whole: the definition's argument.

hosts.description: The hosts the adapter answers for: the definition's hosts, the most an answer may claim.
